title: BUDGET AND FINANCE COMMITTEE REPORT relative to the acceptance of the 2026-2027 Juvenile Justice Crime Prevention Act (JJCPA) grant award from the Los…
text:
[Council File 26-1466]
[Items for which Public Hearings Have Not Been Held - (10 Votes Required for Consideration)]
BUDGET AND FINANCE COMMITTEE REPORT relative to the acceptance of the 2026-2027 Juvenile Justice Crime Prevention Act (JJCPA) grant award from the Los Angeles County (County) Probation Department to support the Juvenile Re-Entry Partnership Program.
Recommendations for Council action, SUBJECT TO THE APPROVAL OF THE MAYOR:
1. NOTE and FILE the Mayor’s Office of Gang Reduction and Youth Development report dated October 13, 2026, attached to the Council file.
2. AUTHORIZE the Mayor, or designee, to:
a. Accept the 2026-27 JJCPA grant in the amount of $2,400,000 from the County Probation Department to support the Juvenile Re-Entry Partnership Program for the performance period from October 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.
b. Submit any other necessary agreements and documents relative to the implementation of this program, subject to the review and approval of the City Attorney as to form and legality.
c. Negotiate and execute contracts with five community-based organizations listed below for a nine- month term within the grant performance period for a combined total amount not to exceed $1,637,889 to provide juvenile re-entry services, subject to the approval of the City Attorney as to form and legality and compliance with the City’s contracting requirements:
i. El Centro del Pueblo, Central Regional Service Area: $327,577.80 ii. Homeboy Industries, Central Regional Service Area: $327,577.80 iii. Alliance for Community Empowerment (Sole-Source), Valley Regional Service Area:
$327,577.80 iv. Soledad Enrichment Action, South Regional Service Area: $327,577.80
v. Watts Labor Community Action Committee, South Regional Service Area: $327,577.80
d. Negotiate and execute a sole-source contract with the Loyola Marymount University to provide data evaluation services for a nine-month term within the grant performance period for a total amount not to exceed $200,000, subject to the approval of the City Attorney as to form and legality and compliance with the City’s contracting requirements.
e. Negotiate and execute a contract with one community-based organization to provide training for a nine-month term within the grant performance period for a total amount not to exceed $200,000, subject to the approval of the City Attorney as to form and legality and compliance with the City’s contracting requirements.
3. Approve the funding allocation of the JJCPA grant award in the total amount of $2,400,000 to implement the Re-Entry Program for the period from October 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, as follows:
a. Salaries and Benefits: $362,111
b. Service Provider Contracts: $1,637,889
c. Evaluation/Data Collection: $200,000
d. Training: $200,000
4. REQUEST the Controller to:
a. Establish a new interest-bearing fund entitled "2026-27 Juvenile Justice Crime Prevention Act (2026-27 JJCPA) Grant Fund” No. XXX/46, for the receipt and disbursement of JJCPA grant funds, to be administered by the Mayor’s Office.
b. Establish new appropriation accounts within the 2026-27 JJCPA Grant Fund No. XXX/46, in the total amount of $2,400,000, as follows:
i. Account No. 46E146, Mayor: $235,381.57 ii. Account No. 46E299, Related Costs: $126,729.43 iii. Account No. 46E304, Contractual Services: $2,037,889.00
c. Increase appropriations in the amount of $235,381.57 within the Mayor’s Fund No. 100/46, Account No. 001020, Grant Reimbursed, for the reimbursement of grant-funded salary costs.
d. Transfer up to $126,729.43 from the 2026-27 JJCPA Grant Fund No. XXX/46, Account No. 46E299, to the Mayor’s Fund No. 100/46, Revenue Source Code 5346, for the reimbursement of grant- funded fringe benefits.
5. AUTHORIZE the Mayor, or designee, to prepare Controller instructions and/or make technical adjustments as necessary to implement the actions approved by the Mayor and City Council, subject to the approval of the City Administrative Officer (CAO); and, REQUEST the Controller to implement the instructions.
Fiscal Impact Statement:
The CAO reports that the proposed grant activities will be funded by the 2026-27 JJCPA Grant, and the salary costs for the six positions will be offset by available funds in the Mayor’s 2026-27 Adopted Budget. There is no match requirement associated with the grant. There is no additional impact to the General Fund. Financial policies The CAO reports that the recommendations in the report are in compliance with the statement City's Financial Policies in that all grant funds will be utilized for grant-eligible activities.
Community Impact Statement:
None submitted
(Ad Hoc Committee on Unarmed Crisis Prevention, Intervention, and Community Services has waived consideration of this matter.)
